_meta.note: Task 4b (docs/NEXT_STEPS_2026-10.md) -- plain-language definitions for the 'Tax words' library. English only for now: translating this accurately into Hindi/Hinglish needs a Hindi speaker, and the rest of the app has no Hindi locale yet either (see locales/i18n.js). Definitions stay general on purpose -- never 'you should choose X'. A practising CA should review this file after each Budget, same as every // VERIFY figure in tax-engine.js.

regime.plain: The set of tax slabs and rules you're taxed under this year — new or old. Salaried employees can pick either one, most years.
regime.example: The new regime has lower rates but very few deductions; the old regime has higher rates but lets you claim 123 (80C), 126 (80D) and more.

deduction.plain: An amount subtracted from your income before tax is worked out — it lowers the income tax is charged on, not your tax bill directly.
deduction.example: ₹50,000 put into PPF is a Section 123 (80C) deduction — it reduces your taxable income by ₹50,000, not your final tax by ₹50,000.

exemption.plain: A part of your salary that's tax-free outright, before any deduction is even applied — most commonly HRA.
exemption.example: If ₹8,000 a month of your HRA is exempt, that ₹8,000 never counts as taxable income in the first place.

cap.plain: The maximum amount a deduction counts for. Spending more than the cap doesn't lower your tax any further.
cap.example: Section 124 (80CCD(1B)) has its own ₹50,000 cap, separate from Section 123's cap — one doesn't borrow room from the other.

rebate87a.plain: A rule that wipes out your entire tax bill if your taxable income is below a set threshold — a full waiver, not just a deduction.
rebate87a.example: No tax at all if your taxable income is up to {{newRebateThreshold}} on the new regime, or {{oldRebateThreshold}} on the old regime.

tds.plain: Tax Deducted at Source — tax your employer or bank cuts from a payment before it reaches you, and deposits with the government on your behalf.
tds.example: Your employer deducts TDS from every month's salary based on your estimated annual tax.

form130.plain: Your salary tax certificate from your employer — formerly Form 16. It summarises your salary, TDS and deductions for the year.
form130.example: You'll need Form 130 to file your return, and to check your TDS matches what's on Form 168 (26AS).
form130.whereYouSeeIt: Given by your employer; used when filing

ais.plain: The Annual Information Statement — the tax department's own record of your income, from every source it already knows about.
ais.example: Checking AIS against what you've logged here helps catch anything you forgot, or anything the department has wrong.

hra.plain: House Rent Allowance — the part of your salary meant to cover rent. Some of it can be tax-exempt if you actually pay rent.
hra.example: The tax-free portion depends on your rent, your salary, and whether your city is in the higher-exemption tier.

pan.plain: Permanent Account Number — your 10-character tax ID. Your landlord's PAN is needed too, once your rent crosses a threshold.
pan.example: Landlord PAN is required when your annual rent is above {{landlordPanThreshold}}.

itr.plain: Income Tax Return — the form you file each year reporting your income, deductions and tax paid.
itr.example: Most salaried people without business income file ITR-1 or ITR-2.
itr.whereYouSeeIt: Filed on the income tax e-filing portal

taxyear.plain: India's tax year runs 1 April to 31 March — not the same as the calendar year.
taxyear.whereYouSeeIt: Everywhere in this app and on the e-filing portal
